title: Movies with Chaotic Yet Determined Protagonists

commenti.body: Sounds like you’d like to binge Michael Mann’s filmography, but I’d highlight *Thief* as the closest match. The Safdie’s *Good Times* and, especially, *Uncut Gems* are obvious rec’s (point #3 made me think of that immediately). *Training Day* for sure. Heck, *Point Break* for something a little more overtly fun. I’ll wrap up with *Michael Clayton*.

> characters 1) who navigate morally ambiguous situations, 2) Face mounting personal and professional crises, 3) Attempt to craft their own narrative amidst chaos, 4) Display a relentless drive to resolve their problems. any genre, including drama, thriller, and crime works, as long as they feature complex protagonists grappling with chaotic circumstances while striving to maintain control. 

Two obvious picks are *All That Jazz* (1979) and *Bringing Out the Dead* (1999).

If you liked "Match Point," you may love "Crimes and Misdemeanors" from the same director with a very similar plot, although it's a bit sleepier than your other picks.

I also think some great heist movies like Stanley Kubrick's "The Killing," or maybe the Argentine classic "Nine Queens" (nueve reinas) would be a good fit. Nine Queens especially features two protagonists who really are just improvising a solution over and over after things keep going wrong. Another one that might be interesting is the Dylan Kidd film "Roger Dodger" which among other things was the breakthrough role for Jesse Eisenberg and features Campbell Scott in a role similar to what you're looking for.

Collateral is a good one in the Mann oeuvre that might also fit this bill.

Another fun but dumb option: "Cellular" featuring Chris Evans doing his best Tom Cruise impersonation, and Jason Statham as...an LA cop? (famously lampooned by the podcast How Did This Get Made in one of their all time bits: "Jason Statham: Angeleno")

“Buffalo 66” the main character of Billy Flynn fits this almost perfectly. as a main character grappling with childhood trauma and pent up aggression, he goes to the extremes to prove himself right in his convictions about the way he sees the world.

The first movie I thought of is Punch Drunk Love. You’ve probably seen that though. For a double feature you could stay on the Adam Sandler train and watch Uncut Gems. But you’ve probably seen that one as well.

Maybe one you haven’t seen is Margaret by Kenneth Lonergan. This one actually fits your desiderata rather nicely.  I was going to describe it to you, but I think it’s best to watch it without knowing anything at all about it. And watch the directors cut (if you can find it) with the volume turned up loud.
It’s been 20 years since I’ve seen Roger Dodger, but I remember loving that movie.
damn right. havent seen margaret. will check out, thanks!
